context: A single-name event-driven desk inside a multi-manager platform. One PM, two analysts. Horizon is weeks to a few months around a catalyst. Deep primary-source and legal-document work, expert networks, and a risk manager who cuts positions fast. No quantitative research staff and no capacity to build datasets; they consume sell-side, filings, and expert calls. The question is always whether this specific situation is mispriced right now, not whether an effect holds on average.
seed: A hyperscaler was removed as a guarantor on a new SPV with its longstanding chip manufacturer. Is this a sign they are qualifying a second source and pushing risk back onto their primary provider?
plan_A:
**Hypothesis.** Hyperscaler exits as guarantor of an SPV co-sponsored with its longtime chip maker; strategic reading: leverage from an alternative foundry. Exclude ordinary causes; only the residual supports H1. Models: H0-a scheduled release — completion support ending by its terms at substantial completion, tool move-in, first wafer-out, yield/throughput test, or two quarters of DSCR test. H0-b deconsolidation — guarantee as ASC 810 VIE plank → VIE footnote change, deconsolidation gain/loss or step change in unconsolidated-VIE maximum exposure, fiscal-boundary timing. H0-c refinancing/ratings arbitrage — 144A/private-placement takeout or standalone rating → new tranche, rating, spread widening, lower agency-imputed parent leverage. H0-d basket/covenant capacity → revolver amendment, capex step-up, other guarantees trimmed. H0-e partner/regulatory structuring — new equity partner, CHIPS/METI/EU Chips Act ring-fencing, tax. H1 strategic risk transfer → contemporaneous independent qualification at a second supplier, nothing comparable conceded. H2 substitution — finance sub, holdco, keepwell, ECL. H3 souring project — demand shortfall, node slip, insourcing.

**Data.** Original 8-K Item 1.01, EX-10 credit agreement, guaranty, sponsor support/completion agreement: definitions — Guarantee Release Date, Completion, Sponsor Support Termination, surviving covenants. 8-K Item 1.02, amendment exhibit, restated guarantor schedule line by line. EDGAR full-text search, both parties: "released from its guarant", "Guaranty Release Date", "Sponsor Support Agreement", "no longer consolidates", "reconsideration event", "deconsolidat", "keepwell", "equity commitment letter". TWSE MOPS announcements/board resolutions, DART, EDINET (original language). UCC-1/UCC-3; Companies House, Irish CRO, Luxembourg RCS, Dutch KvK, Cayman registries. Rating presale/action commentary. DealScan, Infralogic/IJGlobal, Bloomberg CACS/DDIS. Deliverable: chronology — trigger, date, pre-commitment, replacement support.

**Methodology.** Code 40–60 comparable releases, three strata: semiconductor capacity JVs/fab SPVs; digital-infrastructure SPVs (data center JVs, private-credit build vehicles with residual value guarantees, data center ABS/CMBS); classic project finance (power, LNG, toll). Per case: trigger scheduled/negotiated, in original documents, accounting/ratings consequence, spread change, replacement support, 12-month relationship expansion/contraction, coded cause. Prior written first: mechanical/refinancing dominate, accounting next, leverage-driven one to three in fifty; 20:1–30:1 against H1, ~25x LR needed. Pre-commitment test (falsifier 1). Portfolio sweep: eight quarters of guarantee inventory — guarantees/indemnifications footnote, off-balance-sheet arrangements, purchase obligations table, every SPV/lease vehicle/JV in the 10-K; withdrawals across unrelated vehicles → treasury policy, plus CFO capital-efficiency language. H1 evidence independent of the SPV: customer prepayment/capacity-reservation lines at the alternative; first silicon-proven SerDes/PHY, HBM-controller, chiplet IP on a rival node, 9–18 months pre-product; ASIC design-partner change; MPW/mask-shop activity, reticle customs data; OSAT/packaging-site/second-vendor HBM qualification, available packaging capacity; hiring reqs naming rival PDK, node, DFM flow, mask operations, counted monthly; conference papers, teardowns; 10-K purchase obligations to incumbent. Pricing: SPV spread pre/post release (TRACE, dealer runs, secondary marks) × duration × notional, versus release fee, wafer pricing, equity injection, take-or-pay extension, volume floor.

**Falsifiers, pre-registered.** Condition in signing documents, met on schedule → no signal. Parent replaced by subsidiary guarantor, keepwell, ECL → observation wrong, stop. Guarantees withdrawn across unrelated vehicles in window → treasury policy. Incumbent committed spend rose, or reservation/prepayment within two quarters either way → dependence rising. No independent qualification within twelve months, no available advanced packaging → H1 lacks mechanism. Deconsolidation entry, VIE footnote change at release, CFO commentary → H0-b sufficient. Take-or-pay, volume minimum, residual value guarantee replacing it → risk transfer falsified. First three → confident no.

**Pitfalls.** Legal form vs economics: guarantee, indemnity, keepwell, ECL, residual value guarantee, take-or-pay not interchangeable. Anchoring on the strategic story via noisy hiring/IP evidence. Option vs decision: cheap qualification supports buying leverage, not switching. Timing illusion: foundry decisions precede silicon by two to three years; arrow may run backwards. Press-sampled comparables inflate the strategic base rate; sample filings/databases. H3 externally identical to H1, opposite implications; separate with demand-side evidence, not financing documents.
plan_B:
**H1:** reduced dependence — alternate source qualifying, refusal to back capacity it may not fill, leverage pushing risk onto manufacturer and lenders; expect flat capacity commitments, qualification elsewhere, worse terms to keep the tenant. **H2 (null; modal in sponsor-supported paper):** construction/ramp support springing off a pre-agreed test — completion certificate, COD, two quarters DSCR above threshold, standalone IG shadow rating. **H3:** risk back on as hell-or-high-water offtake, capped guarantee, fronted LC, funded reserve, tool RVG, contingent equity — dodging ASC 810 primary-beneficiary status (obligation-to-absorb-losses prong), rating-agency adjusted debt, purchase-obligations table. H1 only if H2/H3 die, cheapest disconfirmation first.

Documents. Delaware: formation certificate, LLC agreement + A&R — members, capital commitments, class structure (non-voting/tracking), kick-out/participating rights, transfer/put-call. Financing: credit agreement / 4(a)(2) NPA / 144A indenture + OM (notes description, financing-documents summary, risk factors); Guarantee/guaranty article, Sponsor Support, Equity Contribution, Completion Guarantee, Contingent Equity Support, keepwell; release conditions, Project-Completion/COD and DSCR definitions, reserve covenants — as-signed, not conformed. Amendments/consents/waivers, dated: consent fee, margin grid, new covenants, funded reserves, collateral changes; consent solicitation near-dispositive H1/H3 vs H2. Supply/capacity-reservation agreements: minimum volumes, take-or-pay, capacity-corridor flex notice, prepayments, deposit refund/forfeiture, capex reimbursement, tool ownership (consigned/owned/SPV), pricing, MFN, exclusivity, qualification/yield milestones, termination-for-convenience, cancellation ladder, change-of-control, assignment; 601(b)(10)(iv) redactions back-solved from debt quantum, assumed DSCR, counterparty disclosure. Hyperscaler: 8-K 1.01/2.03, ASC 460 note, VIE maximum-exposure-to-loss QoQ delta (best H3 test), off-balance-sheet MD&A, purchase obligations by year, finance-lease/financing-obligation notes, related-party, SEC VIE-consolidation comment letters. Manufacturer: 20-F/local annual report, exchange material-transaction announcements, board capital appropriations, advance receipts, contract liabilities, refundable/guarantee deposits — rising prepayments = substitution. Perimeter: UCC-1s, fixture filings/mortgages, presale reports (guarantee uplift, standalone assessment), later rating actions.

Sizing: pre/post bridge, notional and EL. Notional — principal, payment-vs-collection, cap, interest/breakage/swap-MTM coverage, completion guarantee, unfunded equity, equipment RVG. Post — replacement cap, LC face, debt-service months reserved, NPV of new take-or-pay at SPV discount rate. Expected loss — standalone rating (presale or shadowed off DSCR/contract quality) → through-cycle PD, LGD for narrow-use advanced-node tooling and purpose-built shells, EL transferred, vs incremental release spread: 60–90bp plus funded reserve = real risk moved, unmoved paper = guarantee did little. Cross-check SPV spread vs hyperscaler curve, same tenor, plus CDS both names.

Second source, corroborated independently; qualification runs 18–36 months, so under H1 it precedes the change: alternate-foundry PDK/IP licensing for the design family (EDA/IP vendor disclosures, IEDM/ISSCC/VLSI/Hot Chips papers naming nodes), packaging shift to OSAT/rival flows in substrate/OSAT orders, HBM requalification, test/burn-in bookings, job postings (foundry engagement, PDK enablement, second-source qualification), location tells, incentive awards naming customers, bill-of-lading/trade statistics by HS line/origin. Channel: counsel off-deal — completion or DSCR release standard this vintage, substitutes (reserve, LC, offtake)? syndicate/lender desk — consent solicitation, fee, grid change, secondary selling? ex-planners — forward-year allocation moved, anyone dual-qualifying packaging/substrates? OSATs/substrate suppliers — quoted non-incumbent flow, this family? EDA/IP teams — rival's PDK taken, when? rival foundry — RFQ, node, volume? Two independent sources, different chain nodes.

Validation. Killers: release language verbatim as-signed, test met; no consent solicitation or fee; exposure-to-loss drop below released notional; volumes flat or rising; no qualification predating the change. Any two, no. Base rate: 5–10 same-vintage sponsor-supported SPVs, shared arrangers/counsel.

Pitfalls. Redactions hide the key numbers — back-solve. A second source can coexist with incumbent growth: dual sourcing is about pricing power, not volumes — trade accordingly. Confounders — antitrust/joint-control avoidance, foreign-investment review, export-control attribution, guarantee-fee transfer pricing, thin capitalization. Check the price reaction first. After 300 pages every clause looks intentional; most are precedent.

Output: bridge, dated timeline against qualification evidence, verdict citing documents, and if H1 survives a trade sized to the weakest link, channel work.

gold.preference_rationale: More of a judgement call. These events do not happen often and carry many idiosyncrasies, so it is hard to build a probabilistic base rate and then embed this case into that framework. What this needs instead is a breadth-and-depth search on this particular company: its history with its suppliers, the current industry and competitive context, and the supporting or refuting data points around this specific structure. The mechanism matters, but we are looking at one name for now, so generalization is not what the work has to deliver.
gold.critique_A:
Tries to generalize something that should not be generalized. Coding 40 to 60 comparable guarantor releases treats a set of highly idiosyncratic structures as draws from a common distribution, and the resulting base rate is not a frame this case can be meaningfully embedded in.

The prior it rests on is asserted rather than derived - mechanical and refinancing causes dominate, accounting next, leverage-driven one to three in fifty - and the entire 25x likelihood-ratio bar is built on top of that guess. It reads as discipline but the denominator was invented.

It is also a dataset build, and this desk has no quantitative research staff and no capacity to build datasets.
gold.critique_B:
Focuses on the impact to the numbers and never raises the impact on the prevailing narrative in the market. It sizes notional, expected loss and release spread carefully, but on an event desk the trade often works through how the story reprices rather than through the fundamentals alone, and B has no view on that.

The amount of reading B requires is not a negative - under tenet 10 an AI reader handles the volume - so its pitfall about every clause looking intentional after 300 pages is aimed at the wrong thing. The improvement would have been to say how to separate the data points that genuinely stand out in the reading from the precedent boilerplate that generates false positives: a discrimination rule over what is read, rather than a caution about having read too much.
gold.why_loser_was_defensible: A writes its prior down before looking and pre-registers falsifiers, several of which are individually decisive. An analyst most worried about anchoring on the seed's embedded conclusion would want exactly that structure, and A supplies it where B relies on judgement.
